Applying this standard of review, we find it at least plausible that a physician could read Hikma's press releases
14493: Whether the complaint adequately pleaded that the non-FCC agencies' conduct was authorized for takings purposes; the court held dismissal was not warranted on that ground.

We affirm the Claims Court's determinations that the Communications Act does not displace the Claims Court's jurisdiction and that dismissal is not warranted for want of an adequate allegation that the government conduct at issue was authorized.
14550: Pleading sufficiency under Rule 12(b)(6) for direct infringement of claim 1 of the '862 patent (non-§101 pleading question).
We therefore agree with the district court that Heidary failed to state a claim of direct infringement and as such the claim must be dismissed.
14559: Board granted the government's motion to dismiss for failure to state a claim because the contractor did not plausibly allege the purchase orders were personal services contracts; court affirmed.
we affirm the Board's grant of the motion to dismiss for failure to state a claim.
14577: Pleading sufficiency: Breach-of-contract claim dismissed for failure to state a claim because plaintiff breached the alleged agreement by opposing dismissal of her prior case.
As to Ms. Chisum's remaining breach-of-contract claim against the government, we agree with the Court of Federal Claims that she failed to state a claim upon which relief can be granted.
14634: Rule 12(b)(6) pleading sufficiency of NimbeLink's state-law breach-of-contract claims under the 2015 and 2016 NDAs (nature of confidential information and unauthorized use); dismissal affirmed.
NimbeLink’s complaint fails to sufficiently plead the nature of the alleged confidential information at issue.
14709: Rule 12(b)(6) sufficiency of the tax refund complaint; held it did not plausibly allege an overpayment.
the court held Mr. Pellegrino failed to state a claim because his complaint "provide[d] [no] information about what the estate is, how it earned income, or how it overpaid its taxes."
14768: Rule 12(c) procedure: whether the district court improperly relied on materials outside the pleadings without converting the motion under Rule 12(d); court found any error harmless
Accordingly, we reject Miller Mendel's argument on this issue.
15062: Rule 12(b)(6) dismissal of Count I (OPM/HHS/IHS delegation of Title 38 pay provisions): the Court of Federal Claims improperly relied on documents outside the pleadings, so the claim survives.
Reliance on a document outside the pleadings was inappropriate at this stage of the proceeding.
15063: Rule 12(b)(6) dismissal of Counts III-V (nighttime, Sunday, and holiday premium pay): the complaint plausibly alleges regularly scheduled work, so the claims survive.
Having thus cleared the bar of plausibly stating a claim at the motion to dismiss stage
15130: Rule 12(b)(6) dismissal of the disability retirement claim for failure to state a claim, affirmed.
we affirm the Claims Court's determination that he failed to state a claim for disability retirement.
15212: Rule 12(b)(6) dismissal of the amended complaint for failure to state a claim, on res judicata grounds; court held the claims were properly dismissed.
The Claims Court properly identified the standard for dismissal: A complaint must be dismissed if it fails to state a claim for relief that is plausible on its face.
15238: Sufficiency of allegations that Mint employee Holmes had actual authority to bind the government in the implied contract; held sufficient to survive dismissal.
Thus, Portland Mint's claim is sufficient to survive a motion to dismiss.
15239: Dismissal of claim one for violation of the regulation, on the ground that rights under the regulation are defined by the contract terms; affirmed.

Claim one for violation of the regulation was properly dismissed because where the regulation is designed to create a contract, the rights of a claimant under the regulation are defined by the terms of the contract, thus precluding recovery under the regulation.
15240: Dismissal of claim three for breach of the implied duty of good faith and fair dealing as redundant of the contract claim; affirmed.
the latter claim should be dismissed as redundant.
15241: Dismissal of the Fifth Amendment takings claim because the government's contract breach must be pursued in contract; affirmed.
a party must seek compensation from the government in contract rather than under a takings claim.
15244: Breach of contract claim based on payment of a filing fee was dismissed for failure to state a claim because no contract was plausibly pleaded.
payment of a filing fee alone does not create a contract between the United States and the plaintiff.
15347: Rule 12(b)(6) pleading sufficiency: whether the Board properly dismissed Walsh's complaint for failure to state a claim; the court held the complaint states a plausible claim.

We conclude that the Board took an impermissibly cramped view of the pleading in conducting the necessary inquiry into whether Walsh presented well-pleaded allegations of fact that, taken as true, state a plausible claim for relief under the constructive-change doctrine.
